Cartagena: a colourful façade and vendors on a city street

Transfer to the airport for your flight to Medellín. On arrival, you’ll be met and taken to **Hotel Du Parc**.

After checking in, you’ll start exploring the city. Medellín was founded in the 17th century as a mining settlement. Colombia’s second-largest city is now known as the ‘City of Eternal Spring and Orchids’.

On the tour, you’ll see old churches, narrow streets and historic buildings. Medellín is home to the Metropolitan Basilica, the largest brick church in South America.

Next, we visit the Museum of Antioquia and the large square filled with Botero’s sculptures. Fernando Botero was born in Medellín, and his work holds a special place in the city’s cultural life. This part of the city centre also has spaces to relax, galleries and places for artists to work.

Another well-known part of the city is Comuna 13, a neighbourhood tied to Medellín’s past and the story of Pablo Escobar. Today, it draws visitors from around the world.

The tour ends at El Castillo Museum. Built in 1930 in the Gothic style, the building recalls a French château. The house belonged to Dr Uribe before it was sold to philanthropist Diego Misas, who decorated it with works of art. The mansion later became a museum and cultural centre with a collection of decorative and applied arts.
